property_summary: After accepting ownership, the owner of the contract must be the caller of acceptOwnership.
After calling acceptOwnership() as anyone other than the current owner, the owner does not change (reverts).
The paused() function should return false after initialization and before any pause is called.
Calling acceptOwnership should not revert.
After accepting ownership, the paused state read by paused() is consistent with the state set by pause/unpause.
After calling acceptOwnership(), the owner() always equals the account that accepted.
If royalties for a token have not been explicitly set, getRoyalties returns the default configuration with non-zero royaltyBPS (500) and a valid royaltyRecipient.
For a token that has not been minted or had royalties explicitly set, getRoyalties(tokenId).royaltyBPS is greater than 0.
After acceptOwnership, getRoyalties for any token ID returns a config with royaltyRecipient not address(0).
After acceptOwnership, getRoyalties(0) returns a config with royaltyBPS > 0 if token 0 has not been explicitly set.
If no per-token royalties are set via updateRoyalties, getRoyalties(tokenId).royaltyBPS is 500.
After initialization, getRoyalties for a token without explicit royalties returns a configuration with the default royalty BPS (500 in reference, 1000 in mutant).
After initialization, getRoyalties(tokenId) returns a configuration with royaltyBPS of either 0 (if recipient is 0) or a specific value; the default (no per-token override) must be exactly 500.
After initialization and before any per-token royalty override, calling getRoyalties on any token returns a configuration with royaltyBPS equal to 500.
After initialization, for any token that hasn't had its royalties explicitly set, getRoyalties returns a configuration with royaltyBPS equal to the default (500 in reference, 1000 in mutant).
After initialization, the default royalty BPS for any token without explicit override is 500.
After acceptOwnership, getRoyalties for a token with no custom royalties returns the default royalty recipient as the protocolFeeDestination, not zero address
After acceptOwnership, getRoyalties for a token with no custom royalties returns royaltyRecipient not equal to address(0)
After acceptOwnership, getRoyalties for a token with no custom royalties returns a default royalty recipient that is not address(0).
After acceptOwnership, getRoyalties for a token with no custom royalties returns a default royalty recipient that equals protocolFeeDestination.
After acceptOwnership, getRoyalties for any tokenId returns a royaltyRecipient that is not address(0).
The royaltyBPS of the default RoyaltyConfiguration for any tokenId must never exceed 10000
The royaltyBPS of the default RoyaltyConfiguration for any tokenId must be less than 10000.
After calling acceptOwnership(), the royaltyRecipient address in the default RoyaltyConfiguration for any tokenId must not be cast from a uint32 value.
The royaltyRecipient in the default RoyaltyConfiguration must be a valid address (not address(0) and not derived from uint32).
The royaltyRecipient field in the default RoyaltyConfiguration must be the protocolFeeDestination address set during initialization, not an address derived from a uint32 value.
The owner can always accept ownership if they are the pending owner, and after acceptance, the new owner is the caller.
A call to proxiableUUID always returns the value of the IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT storage slot.
The return value of proxiableUUID() is always equal to the value stored in the IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT storage slot.
balanceOf always returns the stored balance for a given account and token id.
balanceOf does not revert for any account and token id
balanceOf returns the same value when called twice in a row for the same account and token id.
balanceOf is a pure view function that always returns a value, never reverts, and only depends on its arguments; it should return the same value when called twice with the same arguments.
balanceOf returns smaller or equal value than totalSupply for the same id when summed across all addresses
balanceOfBatch returns correct balances for each account and token id
balanceOfBatch returns the same balance for corresponding account and token id entries regardless of the order of accounts or ids.
balanceOfBatch returns the same balance for each (accounts[i], ids[i]) pair as balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i])
balanceOfBatch returns correct balance for each (account, token) pair.
For any set of accounts and ids, the number of elements in the returned array from balanceOfBatch equals the length of the accounts array, regardless of the ids array length.
The length of the array returned by balanceOfBatch is always equal to the length of the accounts input parameter.
The sum of all elements of the array returned by balanceOfBatch equals the sum of balanceOf for each account-id pair from the input arrays.
The length of the array returned by balanceOfBatch is always equal to the length of the ids input parameter.
balanceOfBatch returns an array whose length matches accounts.length when accounts and ids have the same length.
The array returned by balanceOfBatch has a length that equals the minimum of the lengths of the accounts and ids input arrays when accounts.length != ids.length.
